verses.text: “Comfort my people. Give them comfort,” says your God.
“Speak gently to Jerusalem. Tell her loud and clear that her fight is over, her guilt is forgiven, and she's received double from the LORD's hand for all her sins.”
A voice is calling, “Clear the LORD's way through the wilderness! Make a straight, level road through the desert for our God.
Raise every valley. Bring every mountain and hill low. Level the uneven ground and turn the rough places into a plain.
Then the LORD's glory will be revealed, and everybody will see it together. The LORD himself has spoken.”
A voice says, “Call out!” Someone asks, “What should I say?” “Everyone is like grass, and all their glory is like a flower out in the field.
Grass dries up and flowers fade when the LORD breathes on them. People really are like grass.
Grass dries up and flowers fade, but our God's word stands forever.”

You with good news for Zion, climb a high mountain. You with good news for Jerusalem, raise your voice with all your strength! Shout it out! Don't be scared! Tell Judah's towns, “Look, here's your God!”
Look, the Lord GOD is coming in power, and his arm rules for him. His reward comes with him, and what he'll give in return goes before him.
He'll feed his flock like a shepherd. He'll scoop the lambs up in his arm and carry them close to his chest. He'll gently guide the ones nursing their young.
Who measured the waters in a cupped hand? Who measured off the sky with the span of a hand, counted the earth's dust in a basket, or weighed the mountains and hills on scales?
Who ever told the LORD's Spirit what to do? Who advised him and taught him anything?
Who did he go to for advice? Who taught him to judge fairly, gave him knowledge, or showed him how to understand?
Look, the nations are a drop in a bucket, a speck of dust on the scales. He picks up the islands like they weigh almost nothing.
All of Lebanon wouldn't give enough wood for the fire, and all its animals wouldn't be enough for a burnt offering.
All the nations are like nothing in front of him. To him they're less than nothing, like a breath that vanishes.
So who are you going to compare God to? What image could possibly look like him?
A craftsperson casts an idol. A goldsmith covers it in gold and makes silver chains for it.
Someone who can't afford that kind of offering picks wood that won't rot and finds a skilled carver to set up an idol that won't topple.
Don't you know? Haven't you heard? Hasn't anyone told you from the beginning? Haven't you understood since the earth's foundations were laid?
He sits above the circle of the earth, and the people on it look like grasshoppers. He stretches the heavens like a curtain and spreads them out like a tent to live in.
He makes rulers count for nothing and makes the judges of the earth meaningless.
They're barely planted, barely sown, barely rooted in the ground. He breathes on them and they dry up, and a whirlwind sweeps them away like stubble.
“So who will you compare me to? Who's my equal?” says the Holy One.
Look up. Who made all these stars? He brings them out like an army, counting them and calling every one by name. He's so mighty and strong that none of them is missing.
Jacob, why do you say this? Israel, why do you keep saying, “The LORD doesn't see what I'm going through. My God is ignoring the justice I'm owed”?
Don't you know? Haven't you heard? The LORD is the everlasting God, the one who made the earth to its farthest ends. He doesn't faint or get tired. Nobody can get to the bottom of his understanding.
He gives power to the weak and builds up the strength of people who have none left.
Even young people get worn out and faint, and young men fall flat.
But people who wait for the LORD will get their strength back. They'll rise on wings like eagles. They'll run without wearing out and walk without fainting. 🦅
